jobs.title: Senior Geospatial Technician
jobs.description:
The Senior Geospatial Technician is an experienced, hands-on technical role at the heart of our production team. You will work across a variety of lidar processing and mapping tasks, delivering high-quality geospatial products for a diverse portfolio of clients. Comfortable working both independently and alongside an established team, you set a high bar for quality—not only in your own production work but through quality-control functions you perform across the group. As a self-starter, you take ownership of production management, continually looking for ways to improve and innovate our workflows. You are also able and willing to discuss project status and technical details directly with clients, building lasting relationships through consistent, reliable delivery.

Most of all, this is a role built for someone who wants to grow into leadership. You will start as a technical expert and, as you demonstrate impact, take on progressively greater ownership—leading tasks and projects, managing budgets and delivery, mentoring teammates, and ultimately building and guiding a team of your own. We are invested in developing our people, and we will give you the support, autonomy, and opportunities to advance as far as your ambition and ability will take you.

What You'll Do

Perform lidar processing and mapping across a variety of tasks and projects for multiple clients.
Deliver production work to a consistently high standard of quality and accuracy.
Perform quality-control (QC) functions on production work across the team.
Manage your own production—planning, prioritizing, and tracking work to meet schedules and deadlines.
Identify and drive improvements and innovations to geospatial workflows and processes.
Work independently while collaborating effectively with an established production team.
Communicate project status and technical aspects directly with clients when needed.
Build and strengthen client relationships through dependable project delivery.
Grow into task and project management, financial management, and supervision of direct reports.

What You'll Bring

Demonstrated, hands-on experience in lidar processing and mapping.
A strong commitment to quality, with the ability to perform QC on your own and others' work.
Self-starter mindset with proven production-management and time-management skills.
A continuous-improvement orientation—curiosity to refine and innovate workflows.
The ability to work both independently and as part of a collaborative team.
Clear, confident communication skills for discussing status and technical detail with clients.
Interest in growing into project management, financial oversight, and supervisory responsibilities.

Your Path to Grow & Lead

This position is designed as a launchpad. As you establish yourself, you can step into responsibilities such as:

Task and project management—owning schedules, resources, and delivery for your own projects.
Financial management—managing project budgets, scope, and profitability.
Client leadership—serving as a trusted point of contact and growing accounts through great delivery.
People leadership—mentoring, supervising direct reports, and helping build a high-performing team.

jobs.title: Environmental Professional, Biologist and Wetland Specialist
jobs.description:
Wilson & Company, Inc., Engineers & Architects, a national multi-disciplined engineering and architecture consulting firm, is currently seeking a full-time Environmental Professional – Biologist and Wetland Specialist to join our Rocky Mountain Region team in one of our offices in Utah or Colorado. You’ll join our growing team of environmental professionals from across the company to perform biological surveys, wetland delineations, draft reports and site forms, conduct environmental analyses, and deliver quality documents supporting our federal, state, local, and tribal clients under the Clean Water Act (CWA), the Endangered Species Act (ESA), the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), and other applicable federal and state regulations for environmental resource management.

In this position, you will perform fieldwork, evaluate potential environmental impacts and mitigation requirements, and write technical reports for wetland and biological resources on a variety of transportation, railroad, land development, and stormwater/wastewater projects. Biological resources include, but are not limited to, wetland delineation and mitigation, threatened and endangered species, wildlife, vegetation, noxious weeds, and environmental permitting. Aside from biological resources, we will also have you assist in compliance with NEPA and other environmental laws. Strong writing skills are required and experience with GIS is preferred. For the right candidate, this position has the potential to provide rapid growth.

All Wilson & Company environmental staff work collaboratively with engineering professionals in a variety of disciplines across the firm to meet project goals, and with other key staff to build relationships both locally and in all states where Wilson & Company is conducting environmental project work. Strong communication skills are required.

Essential Job Functions

Serve as project and/or task manager for environmental/NEPA projects in Rocky Mountain Region and firmwide; coordinate with and support others for overall project performance and deliver projects to clients on schedule and on budget.
Support the national environmental program through marketing, proposal preparation, and environmental analysis and documentation.
Work collaboratively and communicate effectively with engineering professionals in a variety of disciplines across Wilson & Company to meet project goals, and other key staff to build client relationships in the states where Wilson & Company is conducting environmental project work.
Provide technical environmental resource expertise for wetland and biological resources
Conduct fieldwork as it relates to project needs, includes travel throughout Colorado, Utah, and out-of-state travel to support a national environmental program.
Prepare biological resource reports, including Technical Memos, Biological Assessments, and Biological Evaluations.
Consult with jurisdictional and regulatory agencies and other stakeholders, including the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, etc.
Collaborate on the preparation of environmental and NEPA documentation, in part or in whole, including resource-specific technical reports, EIDs, CEs, EAs, and EISs.
Plan and conduct field delineations of Waters of the U.S., including wetlands, and conduct stream assessments.
Prepare delineation reports, functional assessments, mitigation plans, and Jurisdictional Determinations (JD) requests.
Prepare permit applications under Sections 404/401 of the Clean Water Act and NPDES Section 402.
Coordinate with state, federal, and local regulatory agencies.
Conduct vegetation and species habitat surveys.
Complete database reviews and background research to support NEPA documents and prepare NEPA documentation.
Prepare Section 7 consultations with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.

Required Skills And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Landscape Architecture, Environmental Sciences, Environmental Planning, or a related discipline; advanced degrees preferred
Experience managing environmental projects and supporting NEPA compliance efforts, including technical writing and preparation of environmental documentation, is preferred.
2+ years of experience conducting wetland delineations, threatened and endangered (T&E) species assessments, permitting, reporting, and mitigation planning utilizing the Arid West, Western Mountain, Great Plains, and/or Midwest Regional Supplements. Candidates with 5+ years of experience are strongly preferred.
Experience preparing wetland delineation reports, T&E assessment reports, Section 404 permit applications, and mitigation plans.
Strong field skills in wetland delineation and T&E assessments, including GPS data collection and ArcGIS/GIS applications.
Ability to identify wetlands, jurisdictional waters of the U.S., and associated soils, vegetation communities, wildlife species, and habitats common to the Intermountain West, Colorado, Utah, and Midwest regions.
Experience coordinating with federal, state, local, tribal, and regulatory agencies; Colorado permitting experience and familiarity with CDOT projects is preferred.
Professional certification as a Wetland Professional in Training (WPIT), Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS), or the ability to qualify for PWS certification is preferred.
Proven ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams, manage tasks and budgets, and deliver work on schedule.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and ArcGIS.

This Regional Environmental Manager (REM) is responsible for owning the lifecycle of complex environmental compliance programs across Southern California Amazon Last Mile Delivery Stations.

The REM translates senior leadership vision into executable program frameworks, defines success criteria, and owns the roadmap for implementation across the region.

The REM works with internal and external partners, including government entities, contractors, consultants, designers, construction, operations, and other key stakeholders. This REM will own environmental compliance across up to 15+ Amazon Delivery Stations in the region, with oversight of Multi-Site Environmental Managers (MSEMs) and Environmental Specialists.

Own the lifecycle of complex environmental compliance programs across the region — from strategy through execution and continuous improvement.
Shape regional environmental compliance strategy by identifying emerging risks, analyzing systemic defect patterns, and proposing scalable programmatic solutions before they require escalation.

Position Title

Job Description

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality strives to build and sustain an inclusive and equitable environment that embraces and values diversity. Employees at all levels of the agency work together to foster fairness, equity, inclusion, and belonging. We strive to be a workplace where we share our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals, and while collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations. Visit DEQ’s Civil Rights and Environmental Justice page .

Are you passionate about preserving, enhancing, and protecting Oregon’s environment?
If so, please consider a career with the State of Oregon at the Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ). At DEQ, employees have the opportunity to work with a dynamic and supportive team of mission-focused individuals tasked with maintaining, restoring, and enhancing the quality of Oregon’s air, land, and water.

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has a full-time opportunity available for an Onsite Resource Specialist (Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist / Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Underfill)
in Medford, Oregon.

Please consider joining an innovative team, and work to advance our agency’s mission to protect and improve Oregon’s environmental quality.

About DEQ!

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality is the primary regulatory agency of the government of the U.S. State of Oregon responsible for protecting and enhancing the state's natural resources.

The Water Quality Division’s mission is to protect and improve Oregon's water quality. Protecting Oregon's rivers, lakes, streams, and groundwater quality keeps these waters safe for a multitude of beneficial uses such as drinking water, fish habitat, recreation, and irrigation. This is accomplished by developing and implementing water quality standards and clean water plans; regulating sewage treatment systems, industrial dischargers, and individual onsite septic systems; collecting and evaluating water quality data; providing grants and technical assistance to reduce non-point pollution sources; and providing loans to communities to build treatment facilities.

Over 30% of Oregonians dispose of wastewater from their homes and businesses through the use of septic systems. The siting, design, installation, and ongoing operation and maintenance of septic systems, as well as sewage disposal service licensing, are regulated through the Onsite Wastewater Management Program. Without this oversight, septic systems can fail or malfunction and sewage may be disposed of improperly, thus polluting Oregon’s land and waterways with raw sewage and creating public health hazards.

The Onsite Wastewater Management Program (septic systems) is administered through intergovernmental agreements for 33 counties and is directly administered by DEQ in 3 counties. This position will support Jackson, Josephine, and Curry Counties.

For a visual representation of DEQ’s offices and their locations, view our DEQ Offices and Vehicle Inspection Testing Stations map.

What you will do!

You will serve as an Onsite Wastewater Management Program technical expert in the evaluation, inspection, and permitting of onsite septic systems in Jackson, Josephine, and Curry Counties. Hundreds of onsite applications are submitted to the Medford office each year from individual homeowners, small businesses, and licensed installers. In addition to these applications, the Medford office receives technical questions from the public regarding the program’s requirements and the care and maintenance of septic systems. The office also receives complaints regarding potential septic system violations, some of which can lead to enforcement actions. In addition, local interested parties occasionally request the assistance of the local onsite technical expert to attend meetings and present information.

What’s in it for you!

The opportunity to work in a productive and creative environment where no two days are ever the same! DEQ cares deeply about employee wellness and benefits. We offer a competitive benefits package that offers comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for the employee and their qualified family members, as well as paid sick leave, vacation leave, personal leave, and 11 paid holidays a year. In addition, we offer membership in the Public Employees Retirement System (PERS), and you have the opportunity to potentially receive loan forgiveness under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF). If you are passionate about Oregon's environment, apply today!

This is a full-time, AFSCME represented position.

This recruitment may be used to fill future vacancies.

What are we looking for?

Minimum Qualifications for Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist:

6 years of experience in a natural resource or environmental field
At least 1 year of experience at a technical or professional level performing activities in a natural resource program such as researching and analyzing data, conducting investigations, applying pertinent laws and regulations, or coordinating and monitoring project activities
Registration by the Oregon Health Licensing Agency as an Environmental Health Specialist or Waste Water Specialist. See the Environmental Health Registration Board’s requirements for registration. (Continued employment in this position will be contingent upon the successful applicant maintaining the required registration).
10 hours of soil science courses in Introductory Soil Science, Soil Morphology, Physical Geology, and Geomorphology.

Minimum Qualifications For Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Underfill

6 years of experience in a natural resource or environmental field
At least 1 year of experience at a technical or professional level performing activities in a natural resource program such as researching and analyzing data, conducting investigations, applying pertinent laws and regulations, or coordinating and monitoring project activities

See the Environmental Health Registration Board’s requirements for registration. (Applicants do not need to have current registration at the time of hire, but must demonstrate that they meet the requirements to obtain a trainee registration within 30 days of employment.)

Substitutions

Bachelor’s degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 3 of the required years of experience.
Master’s degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 4 of the required years of experience.
Doctorate degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 5 of the required years of experience.

The underfill option is available to you if you do not meet the minimum qualifications for the Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist upon hire. In order to retain this appointment, you must be able to meet the minimum qualifications for the Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist by obtaining your Environmental Health Specialist or Waste Water Specialist registration by the Oregon Health Licensing Office and by completing 10 hours of soil science courses within 3 years of employment. Continued employment in this position will be contingent upon the successful applicant maintaining the required registration. If hired as an underfill, you will be brought in at the Natural Resource Specialist 3 salary scale instead of the Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist salary scale.

Candidates who are most competitive will also reflect the following desired attributes:

Demonstrated understanding of environmental justice and the historical impacts for marginalized and underrepresented communities; ability to take personal responsibility for increasing their knowledge of environmental justice and diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.
Knowledge and skill in the classification, characteristics, and behavior of soils and the transport of water and wastewater through soils is required.
Knowledge of onsite wastewater treatment system technology and requirements for permitting; experience inspecting and evaluating onsite septic systems.
Experience investigating environmental complaints.
Experience reviewing design plans for new construction, alterations, and repairs of wastewater treatment systems.
Experience regulating sewage treatment systems including issuing permits and authorizations for new construction, alterations, or repairs of onsite septic systems.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to provide clear, concise, and compelling communication of policy and technical information tailored to the needs of diverse audiences; skill in writing and presenting clear and concise reports that include qualitative and quantitative analyses, recommendations, and conclusions to diverse audiences.
Demonstrated experience building and fostering relationships with a diverse group of partners including colleagues, interested parties, communities, organizations, and businesses.

Working Conditions

DEQ believes in a diverse and inclusive work environment. All employees are expected to contribute to a work environment that collectively values and benefits from respecting its diversity and promotes a culture of inclusiveness.

This position will be based out of DEQ’s Medford office; however, the successful candidate may be eligible for hybrid work. The logistics of hybrid work will need to be worked out with the Hiring Manager prior to your hire and may be changed at any time given specific job duties and business needs. DEQ will provide necessary hardware (laptop, monitor, keyboard, mouse, and cell phone) for an employee to successfully work from home. At DEQ sites, you will have access to a workspace, however, it may be shared with other employees.

This position requires frequent travel by car statewide for meetings, trainings, public hearings, conferences, workshops, seminars, and field visits (such as wastewater treatment facilities, land application sites, and spill or complaint sites). During field visits, there is the potential for exposure to pollutants, pathogens or hazardous materials, chemicals, contaminated soil and water, fumes, airborne contaminants, challenging field conditions (steep slopes, heavy vegetation, and uneven terrain), and inclement weather. Evening and weekend work, as well as overnight stays, will occur.

Description

This Regional Environmental Manager (REM) is responsible for owning the lifecycle of complex environmental compliance programs across Southern California Amazon Last Mile Delivery Stations.

The REM shapes and evolves the regional environmental compliance strategy by identifying emerging risks, analyzing systemic defect patterns, and designing programmatic solutions that close compliance gaps at scale. The REM translates senior leadership vision into executable program frameworks, defines success criteria, and owns the roadmap for implementation across the region.

The REM works with internal and external partners, including government entities, contractors, consultants, designers, construction, operations, and other key stakeholders. This REM will own environmental compliance across up to 15+ Amazon Delivery Stations in the region, with oversight of Multi-Site Environmental Managers (MSEMs) and Environmental Specialists.

This is a hands-on leadership position that includes time in the yard and on the floor of busy delivery stations conducting inspections and audits, mentoring MSEMs, ensuring program quality, leading regulatory interactions, and driving accountability across multiple departments and all levels of employees throughout the operation.

Key job responsibilities

Own the lifecycle of complex environmental compliance programs across the region — from strategy through execution and continuous improvement.
Shape regional environmental compliance strategy by identifying emerging risks, analyzing systemic defect patterns, and proposing scalable programmatic solutions before they require escalation.
Design and sustain program controllership mechanisms (business reviews, metric dashboards, escalation triggers) that operate independently without requiring manager intervention.
Independently proxy for the Sr Mgr in weekly and monthly forums (WBRs, MBRs) with full ownership of environmental sections — able to answer, defend, and commit.
Force multiply by designing scalable systems, processes, and training that enable MSEMs and operational stakeholders to execute at higher quality with less intervention over time.
Mentor MSEMs and Environmental Specialists; set the quality bar for root cause analysis and corrective action.
Lead COE/A3 investigations independently to closure with leadership, ensuring root causes explain systemic "why" rather than describing "what."
Own procedures and change management for the region, driving adoption end-to-end.
Lead regulatory agency interactions — including inspections, enforcement responses, and agency negotiations — and drive follow-up requirements to closure.
Manage and oversee local, state, and federal environmental regulations and Amazon policy.
Develop strategic programs by integrating with engineering, construction, and operations. Drive an environmentally responsible culture within the organization.
Ensure work performed by contractors, consultants, and employees is completed in accordance with Amazon standards. Provide comprehensive oversight to 3P environmental vendors and consultants.
Drive environmental metrics — build tools and dashboards that give stakeholders the information they need to make good decisions at scale.
Assess emerging regulations and proactively design mitigation plans before regulatory deadlines create urgency.
Own or coordinate construction and launch activities for new sites within the region to ensure environmental compliance at or before operational readiness.
Represent Amazon at appropriate levels with governmental agencies and throughout the company.
Navigate ambiguity effectively — find paths forward where solutions are not pre-defined and coordinate cross-functionally without deferring decisions upward.

Job Description

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality strives to build and sustain an inclusive and equitable environment that embraces and values diversity. Employees at all levels of the agency work together to foster fairness, equity, inclusion, and belonging. We strive to be a workplace where we share our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals, and while collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status , gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, marital status, age, or physical or mental disability in the administration of our programs and activities. Visit DEQ’s Civil Rights and Environmental Justice page .

Are you passionate about preserving, enhancing, and protecting Oregon’s environment?
If so, please consider a career with the State of Oregon at the Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ). At DEQ, employees have the opportunity to work with a dynamic and supportive team of mission-focused individuals tasked with maintaining, restoring, and enhancing the quality of Oregon’s air, land, and water.

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has a full-time opportunity available for an Onsite Resource Specialist (Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist / Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Underfill)
in Medford, Oregon.

Please consider joining an innovative team, and work to advance our agency’s mission to protect and improve Oregon’s environmental quality.

About DEQ!

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality is the primary regulatory agency of the government of the U.S. State of Oregon responsible for protecting and enhancing the state's natural resources.

The Water Quality Division’s mission is to protect and improve Oregon's water quality. Protecting Oregon's rivers, lakes, streams, and groundwater quality keeps these waters safe for a multitude of beneficial uses such as drinking water, fish habitat, recreation, and irrigation. This is accomplished by developing and implementing water quality standards and clean water plans; regulating sewage treatment systems, industrial dischargers, and individual onsite septic systems; collecting and evaluating water quality data; providing grants and technical assistance to reduce non-point pollution sources; and providing loans to communities to build treatment facilities.

Over 30% of Oregonians dispose of wastewater from their homes and businesses through the use of septic systems. The siting, design, installation, and ongoing operation and maintenance of septic systems, as well as sewage disposal service licensing, are regulated through the Onsite Wastewater Management Program. Without this oversight, septic systems can fail or malfunction and sewage may be disposed of improperly, thus polluting Oregon’s land and waterways with raw sewage and creating public health hazards.

The Onsite Wastewater Management Program (septic systems) is administered through intergovernmental agreements for 33 counties and is directly administered by DEQ in 3 counties. This position will support Jackson, Josephine, and Curry Counties.

For a visual representation of DEQ’s offices and their locations, view our DEQ Offices and Vehicle Inspection Testing Stations map.

What you will do!

You will serve as an Onsite Wastewater Management Program technical expert in the evaluation, inspection, and permitting of onsite septic systems in Jackson, Josephine, and Curry Counties. Hundreds of onsite applications are submitted to the Medford office each year from individual homeowners, small businesses, and licensed installers. In addition to these applications, the Medford office receives technical questions from the public regarding the program’s requirements and the care and maintenance of septic systems. The office also receives complaints regarding potential septic system violations, some of which can lead to enforcement actions. In addition, local interested parties occasionally request the assistance of the local onsite technical expert to attend meetings and present information.

What’s in it for you!

The opportunity to work in a productive and creative environment where no two days are ever the same! DEQ cares deeply about employee wellness and benefits. We offer a competitive benefits package that offers comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for the employee and their qualified family members, as well as paid sick leave, vacation leave, personal leave, and 11 paid holidays a year. In addition, we offer membership in the Public Employees Retirement System (PERS), and you have the opportunity to potentially receive loan forgiveness under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF). If you are passionate about Oregon's environment, apply today!

This is a full-time, AFSCME represented position.

This recruitment may be used to fill future vacancies.

What are we looking for?

Minimum Qualifications for Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist:

6 years of experience in a natural resource or environmental field
At least 1 year of experience at a technical or professional level performing activities in a natural resource program such as researching and analyzing data, conducting investigations, applying pertinent laws and regulations, or coordinating and monitoring project activities
Registration by the Oregon Health Licensing Agency as an Environmental Health Specialist or Waste Water Specialist. See the Environmental Health Registration Board’s requirements for registration. (Continued employment in this position will be contingent upon the successful applicant maintaining the required registration).
10 hours of soil science courses in Introductory Soil Science, Soil Morphology, Physical Geology, and Geomorphology.

Minimum Qualifications For Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Underfill

6 years of experience in a natural resource or environmental field
At least 1 year of experience at a technical or professional level performing activities in a natural resource program such as researching and analyzing data, conducting investigations, applying pertinent laws and regulations, or coordinating and monitoring project activities
Registration by the Oregon Health Licensing Agency as an Environmental Health Specialist Trainee or Waste Water Specialist Trainee. See the Environmental Health Registration Board’s requirements for registration. (Applicants do not need to have current registration at the time of hire, but must demonstrate that they meet the requirements to obtain a trainee registration within 30 days of employment.)

Substitutions

Bachelor’s degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 3 of the required years of experience.
Master’s degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 4 of the required years of experience.
Doctorate degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 5 of the required years of experience.

The underfill option is available to you if you do not meet the minimum qualifications for the Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist upon hire. In order to retain this appointment, you must be able to meet the minimum qualifications for the Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist by obtaining your Environmental Health Specialist or Waste Water Specialist registration by the Oregon Health Licensing Office and by completing 10 hours of soil science courses within 3 years of employment. Continued employment in this position will be contingent upon the successful applicant maintaining the required registration. If hired as an underfill, you will be brought in at the Natural Resource Specialist 3 salary scale instead of the Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist salary scale.

Candidates who are most competitive will also reflect the following desired attributes:

Demonstrated understanding of environmental justice and the historical impacts for marginalized and underrepresented communities; ability to take personal responsibility for increasing their knowledge of environmental justice and diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.
Knowledge and skill in the classification, characteristics, and behavior of soils and the transport of water and wastewater through soils is required.
Knowledge of onsite wastewater treatment system technology and requirements for permitting; experience inspecting and evaluating onsite septic systems.
Experience investigating environmental complaints.
Experience reviewing design plans for new construction, alterations, and repairs of wastewater treatment systems.
Experience regulating sewage treatment systems including issuing permits and authorizations for new construction, alterations, or repairs of onsite septic systems.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to provide clear, concise, and compelling communication of policy and technical information tailored to the needs of diverse audiences; skill in writing and presenting clear and concise reports that include qualitative and quantitative analyses, recommendations, and conclusions to diverse audiences.
Demonstrated experience building and fostering relationships with a diverse group of partners including colleagues, interested parties, communities, organizations, and businesses.

This position will be based out of DEQ’s Medford office; however, the successful candidate may be eligible for hybrid work. DEQ will provide necessary hardware (laptop, monitor, keyboard, mouse, and cell phone) for an employee to successfully work from home. This position requires frequent travel by car statewide for meetings, trainings, public hearings, conferences, workshops, seminars, and field visits (such as wastewater treatment facilities, land application sites, and spill or complaint sites). During field visits, there is the potential for exposure to pollutants, pathogens or hazardous materials, chemicals, contaminated soil and water, fumes, airborne contaminants, challenging field conditions (steep slopes, heavy vegetation, and uneven terrain), and inclement weather. Evening and weekend work, as well as overnight stays, will occur.
